name: EPA

summary.text: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency administers the Clean Air Act and the Superfund programme among other statutes. After the Supreme Court held in Massachusetts v. EPA (2007) that greenhouse gases are air pollutants under the Clean Air Act, EPA issued its endangerment finding for six greenhouse gases on December 7, 2009; the D.C. Circuit upheld it in 2012. On February 18, 2026 EPA published a final rule rescinding the 2009 finding and all federal motor-vehicle greenhouse-gas standards, taking effect April 20, 2026, on the ground that the agency lacks statutory authority rather than on a new scientific finding. The rule was challenged in court on the day it was published. On this site EPA also appears as the agency whose North Birmingham Superfund work was the target of a bribery scheme for which a Balch & Bingham partner and a Drummond Company executive were convicted in 2018.

facts.claim: In Massachusetts v. EPA (2007) the Supreme Court ruled that greenhouse gases are air pollutants under the Clean Air Act and that EPA must determine whether they endanger public health or welfare, or whether the science is too uncertain to decide.
facts.quote: In Massachusetts v. EPA, the Supreme Court ruled that greenhouse gases are air pollutants under the Clean Air Act and that EPA must determine if they pose a danger to public health or welfare.

sources.title: Endangerment Finding timeline
Endangerment Finding: legal basis

facts.claim: On December 7, 2009 EPA finalized its finding under Clean Air Act section 202(a) that six greenhouse gases in the atmosphere endanger public health and welfare of current and future generations, and that motor-vehicle emissions contribute to that pollution.
facts.quote: On December 7, 2009, EPA finalized its finding under Clean Air Act section 202(a) that greenhouse gases in the atmosphere endanger both the public health and the environment for current and future generations.

facts.claim: The 2009 endangerment finding was challenged in court and upheld by the D.C. Circuit in 2012 in Coalition for Responsible Regulation v. EPA.

facts.claim: On July 30, 2025 EPA issued a proposed rule to reconsider the 2009 endangerment finding; the proposal was published in August 2025 with a comment deadline of September 22, 2025.

facts.claim: On September 17, 2025 the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine published a fast-tracked report concluding that EPA's 2009 finding was accurate and is now reinforced by stronger evidence, and that the evidence of current and future harm to human health and welfare from human-caused greenhouse gases is 'beyond scientific dispute'.
facts.quote: the evidence for current and future harm to human health and welfare created by human-caused GHGs is beyond scientific dispute

facts.claim: EPA's final rule rescinding the 2009 endangerment and cause-or-contribute findings and removing all greenhouse-gas emission standards for light-, medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and engines was published in the Federal Register on February 18, 2026 (91 FR 7686, docket EPA-HQ-OAR-2025-0194), with an effective date of April 20, 2026.

sources.title: Rescission of the Greenhouse Gas Endangerment Finding and Motor Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Emission Standards Under the Clean Air Act
Federal Register Vol. 91 No. 32, document 2026-03157
EPA Rescinds 2009 Endangerment Finding and Repeals Vehicle GHG Standards

facts.claim: In the 2026 rescission rule EPA did not make a new finding that greenhouse gases are harmless; it determined that it lacks statutory authority under Clean Air Act section 202(a)(1) to set vehicle standards over global climate concerns, citing statutory interpretation and the major questions doctrine. The rule did not repeal power-plant, oil-and-gas methane, aircraft or greenhouse-gas reporting rules.

facts.claim: Court challenges to the rescission rule were filed by environmental and public-health organisations on the day the rule was published in the Federal Register.

sources.title: Regulatory Reset: EPA Rescinds 2009 Endangerment Finding, Repeals Greenhouse Gas Vehicle Standards

facts.claim: In Environmental Defense Fund v. Wright the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts ruled on September 17, 2025 that the Department of Energy's Climate Working Group did not fall within the Federal Advisory Committee Act exception for groups assembled to exchange facts, and in a January 30, 2026 final judgment declared that the group was a federal advisory committee that provided substantive policy advice to DOE; the court dismissed EPA as a defendant, finding no persuasive evidence of FACA violations outside DOE.
facts.quote: Climate Working Group was a Federal Advisory Committee, and not merely 'assembled to exchange facts or information,' but rather provided substantive policy 'advice and recommendations' to the Department of Energy

sources.title: Environmental Defense Fund, Inc. v. Wright
Court Rules Trump Administration's Secret 'Climate Working Group' Violated Federal Law

facts.claim: After EPA notified a Drummond Company subsidiary of potential liability for cleanup costs at the North Birmingham Superfund site, Balch & Bingham partner Joel Gilbert and Drummond vice president David Roberson bribed Alabama Representative Oliver Robinson, through a $360,000 consulting contract with his foundation, to advocate Drummond's opposition to EPA's prioritisation or expansion of the site; a federal jury convicted both in 2018 and the Eleventh Circuit affirmed.
facts.quote: cast a vote for a state resolution drafted by Gilbert opposing the EPA's efforts

connections.claim: Environmental Defense Fund and the Union of Concerned Scientists sued Energy Secretary Chris Wright, DOE, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin and EPA over DOE's Climate Working Group report; the court found FACA violations by DOE and Secretary Wright and dismissed EPA as a defendant.
connections.quote: no persuasive evidence of conduct violative of the FACA on the part of any entity outside of the Department of Energy and Secretary Wright

connections.claim: Claimants of the section 45Q carbon-capture credit must have an EPA-approved monitoring, reporting and verification plan; TIGTA found in April 2020 that 87 percent of credits claimed by the ten largest claimants were claimed without one in place.

sources.title: TIGTA Says Numerous Improper Carbon Oxide Credits Claimed

openQuestions: Site claim that EPA repealed the endangerment finding and all federal vehicle greenhouse-gas standards in February 2026 is supported (91 FR 7686, published February 18, 2026).

Site claim that a federal court ruled the DOE group violated advisory-committee law is supported (EDF v. Wright, D. Mass., final judgment January 30, 2026); the court dismissed EPA itself as a defendant.
Site claim that the National Academies called the evidence of harm 'beyond scientific dispute' is supported (report of September 17, 2025).

Site claim that EPA's final rule 'dropped the DOE report and relied on legal arguments' is partly supported: law-firm summaries confirm the final rule rests on statutory authority rather than a new scientific finding, but none of the sources found states explicitly that the DOE report was dropped from the final rule's basis. The owner may wish to check the final rule text.

Site claim that a 'DOE report by five contrarian scientists backed the proposal' was not tested here; the number and identity of the Climate Working Group authors were not found in the sources opened.
The current status of the D.C. Circuit challenge (APHA v. EPA, No. 26-1037, per the site) was not checked.
